title: Two chiral tetradecanuclear hydroxo-lanthanide clusters with luminescent and magnetic properties

material_class.structural_family: chiral tetradecanuclear hydroxo-lanthanide cluster; [Dy6(μ3-OH)8] octahedron sharing two opposing apexes with two [Dy5(μ4-OH)(μ3-OH)4] square pyramids

synthesis.procedure: An aqueous solution of NH4acac (75 mL, 2 mol/L) was added slowly with stirring to a solution of 0.1 mmol DyCl3·6H2O (0.38 g) in 10 mL cold water. NH3·H2O (1.0 M) was added to keep pH 7.0–7.5, producing a white precipitate. Stirring was continued for about 5 hours. The white precipitate was filtered, washed with water and air-dried (about 67% yield based on DyCl3). Block colorless crystals of 1 were obtained by recrystallization from CH2Cl2/petroleum ether mixed solvents (10 mL; petroleum ether boiling range 60–90 °C) at room temperature after three days.
synthesis.temperature: cold water for precipitation; recrystallization at room temperature
synthesis.time: stirring about 5 hours; crystals after three days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous ligand-controlled hydrolysis followed by recrystallization from mixed solvents
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: white precipitate filtered, washed with water, air-dried; recrystallized from CH2Cl2/petroleum ether to give block colorless crystals

properties.summary: χmT at 300 K is 191.55 emu K mol−1 (slightly below 198.38 emu K mol−1 expected for 14 independent Dy3+), dropping to 110.3 emu K mol−1 at 1.8 K; no AC frequency dependence/SMM behavior. Solid-state photoluminescence under 340 nm excitation shows Dy3+ characteristic blue/yellow emission at 485 and 575 nm (near-white); the detailed PL paragraph in the paper swaps labels 1/2, but the summary assigns near-white emission to the Dy cluster.

measurements.name: emission maxima
measurements.conditions: solid state, λex = 340 nm, room temperature; 4F9/2 → 6HJ (J = 15/2, 13/2) of Dy3+

source_locations.location: experimental synthesis of 1; narrative synthesis paragraph

material_class.structural_family: isostructural chiral tetradecanuclear hydroxo-lanthanide cluster; [Tb6(μ3-OH)8] octahedron sharing two opposing apexes with two [Tb5(μ4-OH)(μ3-OH)4] square pyramids

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the same procedure as 1, substituting TbCl3·6H2O (0.1 mmol, 0.37 g) for DyCl3·6H2O. White solids obtained in about 71% yield (based on TbCl3). Block colorless crystals of 2 obtained by the same CH2Cl2/petroleum ether recrystallization as 1.
synthesis.temperature: cold water for precipitation; recrystallization at room temperature
synthesis.time: stirring about 5 hours; crystals after three days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous ligand-controlled hydrolysis followed by recrystallization from mixed solvents
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: white solids isolated analogously to 1; recrystallized from CH2Cl2/petroleum ether to give block colorless crystals

properties.summary: χmT at 300 K is 161.32 emu K mol−1 (below 165.48 emu K mol−1 for 14 noninteracting Tb3+), decreasing to 50.9 emu K mol−1 at 1.8 K, attributed to Stark-level depopulation. Solid-state photoluminescence under 340 nm excitation shows Tb3+ characteristic bands at about 490, 545, 585 and 620 nm (5D4 → 7FJ, J = 6–3), strongest at 545 nm giving bright green emission; the detailed PL paragraph swaps 1/2, but the summary assigns green emission to the Tb cluster.

measurements.name: emission maxima
measurements.conditions: solid state, λex = 340 nm, room temperature; 5D4 → 7FJ (J = 6, 5, 4, 3) of Tb3+; strongest ~545 nm
